content: Globally, the incidence of neural tube defects is approximately 2 to 6 cases per 1,000 live births. Pregnant women who are taking medications to manage epilepsy are at an increased risk of having a child with a neural tube defect. Additionally, research has demonstrated that women with deficiencies in folic acid are more likely to have a child affected by a neural tube defect. However, folic acid deficiency is only one contributing factor. While taking folic acid supplements does not entirely eliminate the risk of neural tube defects, it significantly reduces the likelihood of their occurrence. In Canada, the mandatory fortification of certain foods with folic acid has been shown to decrease the incidence of neural tube defects by 46%. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant are strongly advised to take daily folic acid supplements unless their regular dietary intake of folic acid is already sufficient. Neural tube defects can be identified through various methods, including prenatal screening tests and medical imaging techniques. In many cases, these defects are visibly apparent at birth. However, some occult neural tube defects may remain undiagnosed until later in life. There are several types of neural tube defects, including: Anencephaly: A severe defect where major portions of the brain and skull fail to develop.
